items.reason: Needs network: pinning an action to a SHA means asking GitHub what the tag points at right now, and inventing a digest breaks the workflow rather than pinning it — the repo already ships the resolver (`npm run actions:pin`, scripts/actions-pin.mjs) and it is documented as needing network.

Already fenced another way: scripts/commit-subject.mjs refuses every family in the sampled log (first-person, opens-with-done, loop-mechanics, run-progress, item-tally, queue-position), rubric A5 runs it over origin/master..HEAD in check:ci and in agent-review.yml on every push AND pull request, and `npm run commit:check -- --message` exists as documented; what remains is history, which cannot be rewritten from this session.

Already covered: AGENTS.md § 'Which of these rules will actually stop you' is a 50-row rule-to-fence table with a `rung` column (blocking / reporting / partial / honour), backed by .github/constraint-map.json and held to the tree by test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs — the eslint.config.mjs sentence the scan quotes is the historical reason the fences were added, in the past tense.

Needs a build run: the route-cost half is already fenced (.github/perf-budgets.json + tests/perf-budget.spec.ts in the required E2E job), and the half still open is bundle size, which requires `next build` output to declare a defensible ceiling — the `.next/` in this worktree is a stale dev artefact with no chunks, and a ceiling invented without measuring is exactly what perf-budgets.json's own `notCovered` note refuses.

Already covered: scripts/lib/review-prompt.mjs fences all four untrusted surfaces of the reviewer's prompt (commit messages, PR body, Part A report, the DIFF) behind a per-run nonce with a system prompt saying an instruction inside the fence is a finding; test-unit/prompt-injection.test.mjs runs the committed hostile corpus on every build and .github/workflows/llm-drift.yml runs `injection-drill --live` weekly.

Added `npm run check:fast`, an inner loop derived from the declared chain (the fourteen `seconds` stages of scripts/gate-remedy.mjs, then typecheck, lint and the already-existing scoped `test:fast`), skipping `next build` and the 499-file suite and printing what it skipped every time; test-unit/check-fast.test.mjs blocks if it stops being a strict subset or is wired into check:ci or the pre-push hook.

scripts/lint-fence-drill.mjs lints thirteen fixtures through the real ESLint against this repository's own config — violations that each fence must refuse and the code each fence deliberately allows — and test-unit/lint-fence-firing.test.mjs blocks on it inside test:unit, including a negative control that re-runs every case with the `adamant/*` blocks removed and requires a red, plus a census so a fourth fence cannot land unrehearsed.

Added the reverse lookup docs/task-index.md never had: .github/adr-ownership.json maps every one of the twelve ADRs to the paths it governs, `npm run adr:owner -- <path>` answers with a path instead of a task, and test-unit/adr-ownership.test.mjs blocks when a record has no row or a row names a path that has moved; `--unmapped` reports the subtrees no record claims, deliberately without a number.

lessons: This repository states, for every rule, whether anything actually enforces it (.github/constraint-map.json and AGENTS.md's rung table) — read that table before proposing a fence, because roughly half the gaps a maturity scan raises here are already fenced and the scan is reading a snapshot that predates the fence.

AGENTS.md and docs/task-index.md sit EXACTLY on their line ceilings in .github/guidance-budget.json (`wc -l` them first). Adding guidance is a deliberate two-part diff — the paragraph, plus the per-file ceiling, the total, and a dated `$raised` note saying why every run should now read it.

Assertions here are overwhelmingly text-level (does the config still say X?), which is blind to a rule that is still written and has stopped matching. When strengthening a fence, prefer running the real tool over a fixture and pair it with a negative control that removes the fence and requires a red — the repo already uses that shape in test-unit/contract-ledger-ceiling.test.mjs and test-unit/prompt-injection.test.mjs.

An Ascent lane in a throwaway worktree runs no hooks, so the outer harness's commit subject is the one thing the repository cannot refuse before it is written: rubric A5 (scripts/commit-subject.mjs) rejects 'partial work from an interrupted lane session' and 'Done. Here's what I found' by name, so the report's first line has to be written as a conventional-commit subject.
